### Spiritual Amnesia
Author: Pastor Jeff Schreve
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/fromhisheart/from-his-heart-week-of-july-8-2016.html
Passage: Psalm 106:13
Points:
- Spiritual amnesia occurs when believers quickly lose sight of the wondrous works God has done.
- Even after experiencing the miraculous parting of the Red Sea, Israel grumbled only days later.
- Practicing personal journaling helps document God's answers to prayer and preserves spiritual memory.
- Remembering God's past track record gives believers confidence that He will carry them through present trials.

### Sometimes I Forget
Author: Gwen Smith
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/girlfriends/girlfriends-in-god-june-9-2023.html
Passage: Psalm 106:13
Points:
- Everyday human forgetfulness mirrors the deeper problem of forgetting God's past kindnesses.
- The Israelites witnessed extraordinary deliverances yet rapidly drifted into grumbling and testing the Lord.
- Spiritual forgetfulness leads to impatience with God's timing and indulgence of fleshly cravings.
- Believers must make intentional efforts to remember God's faithfulness and maintain responsive gratitude.

### A Call for God to Remember
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/call-god-remember
Passage: Psalm 106:1–5
Points:
- The psalmist offers a clear biblical model for approaching God in prayer with praise and petition.
- Believers should prioritize regular thanksgiving for God's inherent goodness and saving mercy.
- True prayer acknowledges God's covenant salvation, which finds its ultimate fulfillment in Jesus Christ.
- Crying out for divine favor rests entirely upon God's grace rather than human merit.

### Holding Both Beautiful and Brutal
Author: Victoria Loorz
Site: The Upper Room
URL: https://www.upperroom.org/disciplines/en-2026-10-07
Passage: Psalm 106:1–6, 19–23
Points:
- Scripture invites believers to acknowledge painful stories of human failure alongside God's enduring love.
- Opening with praise, the psalm moves promptly to transparent corporate confession of sin.
- Recalling past transgressions like the golden calf guards against self-righteousness.
- Moses standing in the breach highlights the vital role of intercession and God's willingness to show mercy.
